GENCTRLGeneric Clock Generator Controlp. 128

offset 0x4 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W · write-protected, write-synchronized

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
21RUNSTDBYR/W0Keeps the generator running in standby when it drives its GCLK_IO pin; with GENCTRL.OE at 0 it has no effect and the generator runs only when a peripheral asks for its clock.
0Generator stops in standby; GCLK_IO holds the level set by GENCTRL.OOV.
1Generator keeps running and driving GCLK_IO in standby.
20DIVSELR/W0Picks how the generator divides its source. For no division, DIVSEL must be 0 and GENDIV.DIV for that generator 0 or 1.
0Source divided by GENDIV.DIV.
1Source divided by 2^(GENDIV.DIV+1).
19OER/W0Drives the generator's clock out on GCLK_IO, when GCLK_IO is not chosen as a source in GENCTRL.SRC.
0No output.
1Output on GCLK_IO, unless that GCLK_IO is the selected source.
18OOVR/W0Level of GCLK_IO while it carries no clock, when GCLK_IO is not chosen as a source in GENCTRL.SRC.
0GCLK_IO low while the generator is off or OE is 0.
1GCLK_IO high while the generator is off or OE is 0.
17IDCR/W0Evens out the generator's duty cycle for odd division factors.
0Duty cycle uneven for odd division factors.
150/50 duty cycle.
16GENENR/W0Turns the generic clock generator on or off.
0Generator off.
1Generator on.

offset 0x02 · per channel, every 0x10 · 16 bits · access -

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15:0BTCNT-x16-bit block transfer count. The internal counter drops by 1 after each beat and is written to the channel's write-back location when the channel loses priority, is suspended or is disabled (by transfer completion, a transfer error or software).

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
31:0SRCADDR-0x0Source address of the block. With BTCTRL.SRCINC=0 it is the address of the block's last beat. With SRCINC=1 it is SRCADDRSTART + BTCNT·(BEATSIZE+1)·2^STEPSIZE when BTCTRL.STEPSEL=1, and SRCADDRSTART + BTCNT·(BEATSIZE+1) when STEPSEL=0; SRCADDRSTART is the first beat's source address, BTCNT the starting number of beats left, BEATSIZE the bytes per beat setting, STEPSIZE the beats per step.

NVMCTRLNonvolatile Memory Controllerp. 364

CTRLAControl Ap. 365

offset 0x00 · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W · pac write-protection

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15:8CMDEXR/W0x0Writing the key 0xA5 here runs the command in CMD; the key and CMD must be written together. Any other value is refused and sets STATUS.PROGE, which is also set when an earlier command has not finished. INTFLAG.READY must be 1 when a command is issued. An APB command arriving in the same cycle as an AHB access waits until the NVM block and AHB are idle, the AHB access going first. Bit 0 of CMDEX reads 1 until the command is issued. ADDR.ADDR is a 16-bit (half-word) address.
6:0CMDR/W0x0Selects the command that runs when the CMDEX key is written.
0x00-0x01-Reserved.
0x02ERErase Row: erases the main-array row at ADDR.
0x03-Reserved.
0x04WPWrite Page: copies the page buffer into the page at ADDR.
0x05EARErase Auxiliary Row: erases the auxiliary row at ADDR; allowed only on the User Configuration Row and only while the Security bit is clear.
0x06WAPWrite Auxiliary Page: copies the page buffer into the page at ADDR; allowed only on the User Configuration Row and only while the Security bit is clear.
0x07-0x0E-Reserved.
0x0F-Reserved.
0x1A-0x19-Reserved.
0x1ARWWEEERRWWEE Erase Row: erases the RWWEE-array row at ADDR.
0x1B-Reserved.
0x1CRWWEEWPRWWEE Write Page: copies the page buffer into the RWWEE-array page at ADDR.
0x1D-0x3F-Reserved.
0x40LRLock Region: locks the region holding the ADDR location.
0x41URUnlock Region: unlocks the region holding the ADDR location.
0x42SPRMTurns Power Reduction mode on.
0x43CPRMTurns Power Reduction mode off.
0x44PBCPage Buffer Clear: empties the page buffer.
0x45SSBSet Security Bit: turns security on by putting 0x00 in byte 0 of the lockbit row.
0x46INVALLMarks every cache line invalid.
0x47LDRLock Data Region: locks the data region holding the ADDR location; with the security extension enabled, secure regions are locked only by a secure access.
0x48UDRUnlock Data Region: unlocks the data region holding the ADDR location; with the security extension enabled, secure regions are unlocked only by a secure access.
0x47-0x7F-Reserved.

10:0ADDRR/W0x0Writing an address starts a transfer that depends on the bus state. UNKNOWN: INTFLAG.MB and STATUS.BUSERR set and nothing more happens. BUSY: the host waits for IDLE. IDLE: the host sends a start and the address; on an ACK it holds SCL low and sets STATUS.CLKHOLD and INTFLAG.MB. OWNER: a repeated start follows, preceded by the acknowledge action if the last transfer was a read; this write is made with one of the SB or MB flags of INTFLAG set. The write clears the BUSERR and ARBLOST bits of STATUS and the MB and SB flags of INTFLAG. Reading ADDR never disturbs the bus. Bit 0 is the R/W bit: 0 write, 1 read.

0x0NFRQNormal frequency: TOP = PER, update at TOP/ZERO, output toggles on match, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.
0x1MFRQMatch frequency: TOP = CC0, update at TOP/ZERO, output toggles on match, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.
0x2NPWMNormal PWM: TOP = PER, update at TOP/ZERO, output set on match and cleared on update, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.
0x3ReservedReserved.
0x4DSCRITICALDual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at ZERO counting down.
0x5DSBOTTOMDual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at ZERO counting down.
0x6DSBOTHDual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at TOP and ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.
0x7DSTOPDual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at TOP counting up.
